::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Oct 13th 1863  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 3-4
:::

[Sir](people/person_939.qmd),

I am obliged for your letter of the 9th. The MS of the [Clever Woman of the Family](cmy_books/cmybook_58.qmd) is not sufficiently forward for the calculations for printing to be made yet. I have however a tale called '<u>[the Trial](cmy_books/cmybook_53.qmd)</u>' which has been coming out in the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd), where it will be completed in the early spring when I should wish to bring it out, but it ought to be uniform with the '<u>[Daisy Chain](cmy_books/cmybook_24.qmd)</u>' as it is in some degree a continuation. If you think it worth while to make any calculations regarding it so long beforehand, I will send you as much as is printed, which is by far the greater part.

I should prefer the arrangement you propose of receiving a fixed sum for each edition. With regard to my other works I have long thought it would be well to bring out a cheap edition, but [Messrs Parker](organizations/other_152.qmd) were averse to so doing, and I think it may be a difficulty that all the books are in stereotype, so that there can hardly be a change of size in a new edition.

I find that [Mr Parker](people/person_1144.qmd) has made over his interest in my works to Messrs [Longman](organizations/other_153.qmd), to whom I wrote to enquire various particulars as to terms and as to the price they would set upon the half profits of the [Heir of Redclyffe](cmy_books/cmybook_15.qmd) and [Heartsease](cmy_books/cmybook_19.qmd). In answer they say that they will take 'the earliest opportunity of replying to my question.' When I have received this reply, I shall hope to communicate with you again 

Your obt servt 

C.M. Yonge
